items.title: Natty Dominique Interview, 1958-05-31
items.q: I played a picnic right alongside of Joe.

ctx.x: Well, there's a couple other fellas here on the list. Joe Oliver, can you tell us what kind of a fella he was?

Fine fella. Swell guy. Full of fun. I work right opposite. Louie and I work opposite. And don't think, cause Louie and I was across the street. Joe Oliver had Bob Schauffer. And he also had Kid Ory. He had Joyce Field there, too. He had Kid Ory with him. Don't think the plantation was packed. Like our place was packed. Both in cabaret right opposite each other. It was packed. Danny had the apex across the street after hours. All the places would be packed. It was a good day. Yeah, it was a good day. Bob Schauffer…
Same Bob Schauffer. Now, Joe was full of fun. Full of fun.

items.title: Natty Dominique Interview, 1958-05-31
items.q: I heard Johnny up here at the Royal Garden with King Oliver.

ctx.x: Hold on, I don't hurt, the storm won't hurt that I don't think. Well, that kind of... Instead of picking up all the rain, you hear the rain on here and the, uh, thunder. I guess that won't be the tornado they predicted maybe anyway, we hope not.

So, them kind of fellas, I can tell you a lot about them, because I know them, I work with majority of them. Now we couldn't come to Jimmy Noon. I work with Jimmy Noon. My last recording on the deck was, you remember, with Jimmy Noon. Jimmy Noon and everybody. Johnny Dotson. My last recording on the deck. Johnny Dotson and Jimmy Noon. Jimmy Noon's a good musician. Read clarinet parts like nobody's business. I mean clarinet parts. And Johnny Dots could read clarinet parts. Very few clarinet parts you can find read…
Barney is your cousin. My cousin.

items.title: Natty Dominique Interview, 1967-11-15
items.q: Well, they didn't let us put up that brass band of Louis, myself, King Oliver, and Lee Collins, and Oliver. We had a gang of us.

ctx.x: He said, why you didn't tell him you told him you were saxophone player? He said, I play sax. But I heard you practicing downstairs. That was enough for me. So I'm going to play clandest.

He said, no Bonnie, no contest. Monica, I'm scared of it. Just practicing. Sweet dream. Coleman Hawkins had everybody buying my pieces like his. Couldn't produce his stuff. And you never hear, when he plays a number, you never hear a squeak note. Smooth. Same thing with Dutre. You already Dutre? I already Dutre. Smooth. Smooth. John Bone. John Bone. Ferris Smooth. Great musician. We had good, we had good, all of us now to read music. Because you have to read music when you come to Chicago from New Orleans because…
the parades away from us now? What's that? A street band?
